reference_role: Existing illustration atlases preserve identities; newly generated item pixel atlas sets style. All final sprites originate from new generated pixel-art atlases.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: nine true low-resolution fantasy pixel-art game item sprites, presented together as one 3-column by 3-row atlas.
Input image 1 is an identity/color/subject reference ONLY. Redraw these as brand-new deliberate 32×32 logical pixel sprites, not a pixelated filter or a resized illustration.
Keep the SAME ordered subjects: row 1 gold coins, red potion with cork, rolled parchment scroll; row 2 bread and cheese, silver sword with gold hilt, gray plate armor; row 3 gold ring with green gem, wooden wand with blue crystal tip, triangular gold amulet with red jewel.
Style: authentic hand-placed 16-bit fantasy RPG pixel art. Each individual sprite should read as an EXACT 32 by 32 logical pixel grid, shown enlarged by uniform nearest-neighbor square blocks. Bold 1 logical pixel almost-black contour, chunky coherent pixel clusters, 2–3 flat shades per material, limited palette, crisp stair-step edges. No smooth cartoon outlines, no antialiasing, no gradients, no painterly microdetail, no subpixel diagonals.
Layout: square canvas, exact uniform 3×3 grid, one centered isolated sprite per cell, generous transparent separation; each sprite fully contained within its own equal cell, no objects touching other cells. Sprites occupy roughly 26–28 of their 32 logical pixels. TRUE alpha transparency around the objects, no checkerboard, no shadows, no floor. No text, labels, numbers, frames, icons, decoration or watermark. Preserve recognizable identities and color roles from the reference.

Use case: stylized-concept. New production pixel-art atlas for Rogue. Input images 1–4 are identity/subject references only: image 1 terrain/player/effect, image 2 monster A–I, image 3 monster J–R, image 4 monster S–Z. Input image 5 is the approved NEW pixel-art item style. Follow image 5's chunky true pixel treatment, never the smooth reference style.
Create deliberate low-resolution 32×32 LOGICAL-pixel sprites shown enlarged as uniform square nearest-neighbor blocks. Each sprite approximately 26–28 logical pixels tall, bold one-logical-pixel near-black outlines, coherent stair-step pixel clusters, flat 2–3 shades per material, low limited palette. TRUE alpha transparency, no antialiasing, gradients, smooth lines, paint, shadows, text, labels, numbers, frames, watermark, or fine noisy detail.
Strict equal-sized atlas cells with ample TRANSPARENT GUTTERS. Every complete sprite stays within its own cell. Preserve silhouettes, major colors, species and characteristic equipment from the relevant identity image; simplify anatomy to clear readable pixel symbols.
Redraw ONLY the 11 terrain/player/effect subjects from image 1. Landscape atlas exact 4 columns by 3 rows. Ordered row1: plain opaque solid almost-black unexplored tile with NO detail, seamless gray stone floor square, seamless darker gray cobblestone passage square, closed brown wooden arched stone door. Row2: horizontally connecting gray stone wall across full logical tile width, vertically connecting gray stone wall across full logical tile height, downward dark stone stairs, generic metal toothed floor trap. Row3: green-hooded sword adventurer, golden four-point magic detection sparkle, orange-gold horizontal magical bolt pointing right, EMPTY transparent cell. The floor/passage tile textures should cover their full square without transparent rims and have consistent edges. All other assets transparent around their pixel silhouette. Show pixel tiles at the same scale as image5's item sprites.
